name: Whiterock House
agent: Gary Quinn, DNG McCormack Quinn, Paul Quay, Wexford
questions: Bedroom 1 on the ground floor is reached only through the 4.46 × 2.56 m family room. Would you or the vendor see any planning issue with moving its door to the hall or adding a garden door, and is the 1.09 × 2.08 m en-suite's shower usable as a level-access shower?

The listing says BER G but gives 418.71 kWh/m²/yr, which is band F. Which is right, and can you share the BER advisory report? Has anyone priced the refurbishment (rewiring, plumbing, roof, windows, insulation)?

Earlier Daft listings for Whiterock House show it went to auction (an AMV of €350,000 in July, then an online auction on 27 October). What happened at those auctions, and is the vendor (estate or private) open to offers at €395,000?
How far does the garden rise behind the house, and where exactly do the folio boundaries run against the neighbouring houses? Is the boundary stock-proof for two dogs?

BuyerIQ shows the site in an EPA High Radon Area and seven large residential schemes about 150 m away. Has a radon test been done, and are any of those schemes (Árd Uisce or others) still to be built next to this site?

ai.why: A 1913 period house on 0.42 ac of screened gardens, walkable to Wexford town and its all-ages ED, with a ground-floor en-suite bedroom, at €395k. But at 154 m² with two bathrooms it is small for six, the parents' room is an 8.7 m² box reached through the family room, and a full refurbishment (rough €150–250k) puts the total at about €545–645k, past the budget, with houses 15–25 m away on two sides.

electricity.detail: Mains; the listing's Services line says 'All main services'. Expect a full rewire in a 1913 house.

water.detail: Mains water; 'All main services' per the listing, on a serviced town road.

sewer.detail: Mains drainage; 'All main services' per the listing. Confirm the old house's drains are connected and sound.

internet.detail: Fibre (per BuyerIQ); BuyerIQ shows '386 Mb full fibre' at Y35 P5V2. The listing doesn't mention broadband; Wexford town has open eir FTTH and SIRO.

groundFloorBedroom.detail: Bedroom 1 (3.27 × 2.65 m) is on the ground floor per the Matterport floor plan, with its own 1.09 × 2.08 m shower en-suite, but it is reached only through the family room and is only about 8.7 m².

bedsNote: Ground floor: Bedroom 1 (3.27 × 2.65 m) with shower en-suite, entered through the family room. First floor: master 5.35 × 4.67 m, 4.13 × 3.89 m and 4.67 × 2.64 m, with the family bathroom on the return
heating: Oil-fired central heating; open fireplaces in the living room and a bedroom
tagline: A 154 m² four-bed 1913 house needing full refurbishment, set back behind mature trees on 0.42 ac on Whiterock Hill, on the south-west edge of Wexford town.

pros.text: Walkable to Wexford General's all-ages ED
pros.detail: Wexford General Hospital on Newtown Road is about 1.9 km in a straight line; the town centre (Bullring) is about 1.4 km and O'Hanrahan station about 1.75 km.
Stamp duty about €3,950; leaves roughly €100k of the €500k line for work before going over (see the refurbishment con).

pros.text: Ground-floor bedroom with its own shower room
pros.detail: Bedroom 1 (3.27 × 2.65 m) has a 1.09 × 2.08 m en-suite with shower, WC and basin, confirmed on the floor plan.

pros.text: 0.42 ac of mature, screened gardens behind a gate
pros.detail: Folio WX40769F shows 0.17 ha; the house is set back up a tree-lined drive with lawns front and side, and the trees hide it from Whiterock Hill.
Bay windows, a 4.36 × 3.97 m bay-windowed porch, a slate hipped roof, fireplaces and a 5.42 × 5.21 m living/dining room.
Gaelscoil Charman is directly opposite, Kennedy Park NS (co-ed) about 400 m, and St Peter's College (boys) about 800 m.
'All main services' per the listing; BuyerIQ shows 386 Mb full fibre.

cons.text: Full refurbishment takes the total past €500k
cons.detail: Rough estimate only: €150–250k for rewiring, plumbing, insulation, windows, a heat pump, kitchen and bathrooms on 154 m² (less any SEAI grants), so about €545–645k all in, before adding a third bathroom.

cons.text: Small for six: 154 m², two bathrooms
cons.detail: 88 m² downstairs and 66 m² up; one family bathroom (2.44 × 1.65 m) serves three upstairs bedrooms and the kitchen is 3.93 × 3.15 m.

cons.text: Parents' bedroom is small and reached through the family room
cons.detail: Bedroom 1 is about 8.7 m² and its only door opens off the 4.46 × 2.56 m family room, so the family room becomes a corridor unless the door is moved; the garden door is in the kitchen.

cons.text: Close neighbours and estates all round
cons.detail: Satellite and the listing's aerial show houses about 15–25 m away on two sides, the Bishopswater and Whitebrook estates beyond, and the school and community centre across the road.

cons.text: BER G (or F) and oil heating
cons.detail: The listing gives 418.71 kWh/m²/yr, which is band F, against a stated G; either way it is a cold, costly house until retrofitted.
Wexford O'Hanrahan has about 4 direct trains a weekday to Connolly, around 2h40.

cons.text: High radon area; new estates nearby
cons.detail: BuyerIQ flags an EPA High Radon Area and seven large residential schemes about 150 m away; its flood finding is behind a paywall.

trips.note: Irish-medium primary directly opposite the house (about 140 m, 207 pupils per Daft); Kennedy Park NS on Whitemill Road (co-ed, Catholic, DEIS Band 2, about 400 m) is the nearest English-medium option.

rating.basis: Its only indexed inspection is a 2009 Whole-School Evaluation behind gov.ie's verification check; gender intake not confirmed (gaelscoileanna are usually co-ed).

trips.label: School run
trips.note: Boys' diocesan secondary, about 780 pupils, about 800 m north; Wexford CBS (boys) is about 810 m.

rating.basis: Named among Wexford's well-placed schools in the Irish Times feeder tables (South East Radio, Dec 2019) and on an older Sunday Independent best-performers list; no recent percentage found.
